title: How Does Counterfactually Augmented Data Impact Models for Social Computing Constructs?
measurement_description: Detection of hate speech directed at religious groups (Jews and Muslims) as part of a broader analysis of model robustness for social computing constructs.
findings: As part of the hate speech analysis, the paper found that models trained on counterfactually augmented data (CF models) learn to better identify core features of hate speech, including derogatory terms targeting religious groups like Jews ('jews', 'jewish') and Muslims ('mussies'). These identity terms were ranked as highly important features for hate speech classification by the more robust CF models, in contrast to non-CF models which learned more spurious or domain-specific features.
